result.title: Human-Oriented World Model
result.summary: Supporting a person over repeated interactions requires interpreting their current state in context and anticipating its subsequent evolution. We formulate the \emph{Human-Oriented World Model} (HOWM) as a conceptual framework centered on task-relevant human states and their evolution. HOWM connects current observations and individual history with environmental and social context to organize continuing state estimation, personalized dynamics prediction, and action support. Dynamic expectations and new observations jointly inform the current estimate, which in turn anchors personalized forecasts based on shared knowledge and individual experience. An external policy relates forecasts under alternative conditions to the person's goals, preferences, and constraints when considering support. Actual responses and outcomes provide evidence for revising the state estimate and personal dynamic patterns, thereby informing subsequent estimation, prediction, and support. We illustrate the framework through hypothetical training and learning scenarios. Our research agenda asks whether accumulated interaction experience improves subsequent estimation and prediction, and whether using the model helps the person pursue their goals over time.

AI.brief_summary: 提出「Human-Oriented World Model」概念框架：以任务相关的人类状态及其演化为核心，结合当前观测、个体历史与环境社会情境，组织持续状态估计、个性化动态预测与行动支持，并用实际反馈修正估计与动态模式。
AI.relevance_reason: 「预测与观测共同更新当前估计、结果反馈再修正状态与动态模式」的循环，与 LVR 中 latent 状态的维护、证据更新和信念抽象结构相近，可供核查；但该文为纯概念议程、仅设想场景且不涉及视觉或多模态推理，实际借鉴价值有限。
